object_description: modular stepped volumes forming a terraced campus framework
design_condition: Two modular volumes occupy the plots and are eroded toward the campus square, with stepped forms adapting to the slope and shaping varied outdoor spaces, but the single central entrance weakens the viaduct-side arrival.

positive.statement: The project consistently interweaves buildings and outdoor space to create an attractive and diverse campus world.
Staggering the volumes ensures good sunlight in the central outdoor spaces.
The central campus square is the heart of the complex and receives all paths.
The topography is made a theme through ramps, seating steps, and stairs.
The weather-insensitive facade construction enables a long service life and reduces life-cycle costs.
The materials are compatible with the specified ecological requirements.

negative.statement: The restriction to one main entrance creates an unfavorable reception situation and long distances.
Important district connections are missing or require large detours, and the viaduct area is unattractive as an open space.
The internal circulation creates long paths, dead ends, and labyrinthine spaces.
The basic spatial-typological rules are unclear and the deviations are not comprehensible.
The huge basement has practically no daylight and many large ground-floor rooms are trapped inside the plan.
Internal access is confusing and inflexible, and the lounge proportions are not optimal.
The complicated volumetrics and extensive facade, terrace, and roof development are complex and expensive to construct and maintain.
The above-average glazing creates a relatively high overheating risk and requires substantial technical effort.
The large supports in the partition walls are inconvenient and the rise zones are limited.
